rationale: Filed a successor of the live-cluster experiment that adds the healing phase, because the current account still lists the post-healing fate of the conflicting entry and the long-run persistence of the stale membership as unobserved. The scenario, admissions, identity fields and the seven existing comparisons are carried over unchanged; the harness now reconnects the full mesh after the split, waits for one leader, applies one more entry and samples the log entry both leaders committed at (index 11, term 3) on all five nodes plus the restarted node's configuration. Local construction feedback is deterministic on those three additions across four runs (entry payloads A:minority-write, C:minority-write against B,D,E:majority-write all at term 3 so the entries cannot be reconciled by term comparison; the restarted node's configuration still {A,B,C} while its log advances to 12; the cluster keeps committing). The healed leader's identity did vary between runs (A once, D or E three times), so no comparison asserts on it; those operands are recorded but not asserted.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} long enough for both sides to elect and commit, and is then healed while sampling the conflicting index and the restarted node's configuration.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations only: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter(D), AddVoter(E) and one further apply.

A is shut down gracefully and restarted from its own store objects; all five nodes run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the persisted commit index the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
The partition and the healing are expressed only by transport disconnection and reconnection in both directions; timings, RPC lifecycles and election rules are untouched.
The healing sample is taken after the sole leader has committed one further entry plus 300 ms; no assertion depends on which node won that election.
excluded: No crash, storage fault or snapshot installation is exercised; the scenario ends with the healed sample.
The fate of the conflicting entry beyond the sampled window (for example after a snapshot install or log compaction) is not observed.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. It starts D and E, adds each as voter through the leader, applies one further command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry, and emits 'fixture' with the snapshot index and membership, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores with the feature on and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome' with leaders, terms, leader count, per-node leader booleans, reported configurations, write errors, write indexes and terms, payloads and the derived conflicting_commits. It then reconnects the full mesh, waits for exactly one leader, applies one further entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' with each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, payload consistency, same_term_conflicting_payload, per-node log last indexes, the restarted node's configuration, B's configuration, the leader's configuration and log index, the number of nodes behind the leader and post_heal_apply_error; all nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed.
semantic_changes: After the outcome sample the harness reconnects every transport pair, waits up to 15s for exactly one leader, applies one further entry on that leader and waits 300ms.

A fourth event 'healed' reports each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, whether those payloads are consistent, whether they conflict at equal terms, each node's log last index, the restarted node's configuration and each side's reported configuration, plus derived operands a_log_advanced_after_heal and nodes_with_log_behind_leader.

Three comparisons are added on the 'healed' event: entry payloads at the conflicting index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership after the cluster runs on, and its log must have advanced.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay; the AppendEntries log-matching rule (truncate only on term difference, skip same-term duplicates) is responsible for whether the divergent entries can be reconciled.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration while both sides lead.
After the partition heals, all nodes must hold the same entry at the index both leaders committed at.
Once the cluster is whole again and committing new entries, the restarted node must use the committed membership.
Progress control: the restarted node's log did advance after healing, so the stale membership is not a stalled state.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a healing phase after the split-brain window and three comparisons over it; the fixture, restart, partition, admissions and the seven earlier comparisons are unchanged.
